Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test `testWriteNonAsciiDirectoryNamePosixMode` in `TarArchiveOutputStreamTest` attempts to write a directory with a non-ASCII name into a TAR archive. The test sets `setAddPaxHeadersForNonAsciiNames(true)` to handle non-ASCII names correctly. The test fails with an exception when trying to write a directory with a name longer than 100 bytes due to an error related to PAX headers. The exception message indicates that the request to write a certain number of bytes exceeds the header size allowed for the entry.

Looking at the provided code snippet, the test creates a `TarArchiveEntry` for the directory with the non-ASCII name and attempts to add it to a `TarArchiveOutputStream`. The failure occurs at the point where the entry is being added to the output stream.

Recent bug reports suggest that issues with handling long file names and PAX headers have been reported before for `TarArchiveOutputStream`.

To pinpoint the root cause, we need to analyze how `TarArchiveOutputStream` handles the writing of directory entries with long non-ASCII names and the management of PAX headers.

I will now inspect the relevant methods in `TarArchiveOutputStream` to identify the potential cause of the failure.
